text.tspan: To give you a feeling for how surprising this is, let's take a closer look.
The segment of DNA highlighted in orange is called a promoter. That's a region of DNA that
transcription factors, in green, bind to to help recruit RNA polymerase and initiate transcription.
When they are bound, this makes it energetically favourable for RNA Polymerase enzyme to
remain attached and kick start the transcription process. Transcripion typically happens in
bursts of many mRNA molecules elongating in rapid succession
